Meta Description: Motorcycle-friendly restaurant in Marlinton WV — home cooking on the Greenbrier River with outdoor deck seating. A rider favorite on the Summersville Loop.
New Full Description:
Casual dining with homemade daily specials and desserts, served in a warm friendly atmosphere. Dining room seats 100 with a deck overlooking the Greenbrier River. Five guest rooms above the restaurant if you need to stay the night. Rider recommended — order the West Virginia Original skillet and grab a bag of corn for the ducks on your way out. A genuine WV experience.

Address: 28 Summersville Lake Rd., Mount Nebo, WV 26679
Meta Description: Motorcycle-friendly campground and retreat on Summersville Lake WV — cabins, RV sites, boat rentals, and West Virginia's only working lighthouse. Perfect base for New River Gorge riding.
New Full Description:
Right off Route 19 overlooking Summersville Lake, this 57-acre retreat is one of the best bases for a Summersville area riding weekend. The gift shop is open 9am-5pm and the staff can point you toward local rides and attractions. The campground is convenient to Summersville Lake, the New River Gorge Bridge, and local stores and restaurants. West Virginia's only working lighthouse is on site — 122 steps to a 360-degree view of the lake and Gauley River National Recreation Area. Dog friendly, motorcycle friendly, and genuinely worth a stop even if you're not camping.

Meta Description: The first US memorial honoring African American WWI veterans, restored and open in Kimball, WV.
New Full Description: Built in 1928, the Kimball War Memorial was the first memorial in the United States built to honor African American veterans of World War I. It sat closed and deteriorating for years before a restoration reopened it in 2006. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Beehive coke ovens ran until 1921. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1992. Off the main Head of the Dragon loop, add it to your own trip if you want the detour.

Meta Description: General store and deli in Slanesville, WV -- stop on the Mountain Store Loop.

Short Description: Built 1853 by Lemuel Chenoweth, a 146-ft Burr-arch span and one of the oldest covered bridges in West Virginia.
New Full Description: West Virginia's second-oldest covered bridge, built in 1853 by the Chenoweth brothers, the same family behind the Philippi span, for the old Fairmont-Wheeling Turnpike over Buffalo Creek. Its modified Burr arch is the longest single clear span of any covered bridge in the state, and for something built by hand in the 1850s it's remarkably sound: it carried real traffic for well over a century with essentially no modern reinforcement. The best story here is why it's still standing at all. On April 29, 1863, during Jones's Raid, Confederate General Grumble Jones meant to burn it, but the Ice family, mill owners and Southern sympathizers nearby, talked him out of it. Two other bridges in the area weren't so lucky.

Short Description: 1856 Burr-arch bridge over the Buckhannon River; gutted by arson in 2017 and fully restored in 2023.
New Full Description: The second-longest and third-oldest covered bridge still standing in West Virginia, built in 1856 by the O'Brien brothers, tied to the Philippi bridge just up the road, spanning the Buckhannon River near Carrollton. It's a 141-foot multiple-king-post Burr arch, and it came close to being lost: an arsonist set it ablaze in August 2017, gutting the roof and siding. The frame held, and West Virginia DOH crews took on the rebuild themselves, reopening it to traffic in 2023. Tucked off US-119 just north of Audra State Park, it pairs naturally with Philippi into a short Barbour County bridge run.

Short Description: Compact ca. 1889 Long-truss covered bridge in rural Doddridge County.
New Full Description: A compact Long-truss span from 1888, crossing the Pike Fork of McElroy Creek in rural Doddridge County. It's one of the smaller, out-of-the-way bridges on the list, the kind you find on a back-road ramble rather than a main route, but a well-preserved example of the plain, sturdy country bridges that once dotted the state.

Short Description: 1889 King-post covered bridge over Dents Run, just north of Morgantown.
New Full Description: An 1889 king-post span over Dents Run, just north of Morgantown near Laurel Point. Small and simple, it's an easy detour if you're riding the northern part of the state, and one of the more accessible historic bridges close to a city.

Short Description: ca. 1881 King-post covered bridge over Fish Creek at Hundred.
New Full Description: Also known as the Hundred Covered Bridge for the little town it sits in, this short king-post span dates to 1881 and was rebuilt in 2001. It crosses Fish Creek in Wetzel County, up in the state's northern reach, a modest, tidy bridge and a quick stop if you're exploring that corner of West Virginia.

Short Description: 1891 King-post covered bridge on a quiet rural road in Harrison County.
New Full Description: An 1891 multiple-king-post bridge over Tenmile Creek on a quiet rural road in Harrison County, sometimes called the Ten Mile Creek bridge. At roughly 58 feet it's one of the larger of the small country spans, and it pairs with the nearby Simpson Creek bridge for a short Harrison County outing.

Short Description: 1884 Queen-post covered bridge on a back road west of Lewisburg.
New Full Description: Built in 1884 for about 800 dollars to serve S.S. Hern's grist mill and the farms across Milligan Creek, this queen-post span sits on a quiet back road west of Lewisburg. It's one of only two covered bridges left in Greenbrier County, and it still carries light local traffic, reinforced with steel stringers back in the 1930s but otherwise little changed. A peaceful, easy-to-reach stop on a southern West Virginia bridge run.

Short Description: ca. 1899 Long-truss covered bridge over Second Creek near Lewisburg.
New Full Description: At roughly 81 feet, Hokes Mill is the longest covered bridge in southern West Virginia, a modified Long-truss span built in the late 1890s over Second Creek near the old mill it was named for. It's the second of Greenbrier County's two surviving covered bridges, quieter and more out-of-the-way than most, bypassed by a modern road and now kept for foot traffic. Worth seeking out if you're chaining together the Monroe and Greenbrier spans.

Short Description: ca. 1898 Howe-truss covered bridge over Indian Creek near Salt Sulphur Springs.
New Full Description: One of the most photographed covered bridges in the state, with one of the best stories behind it: the Indian Creek bridge was built in the early 1900s by two brothers, Ray and Oscar Weikel, who were just 16 and 18 years old, for a county contract of about 400 dollars. It's a Long-truss span near Salt Sulphur Springs, once part of the old turnpike between the springs resorts, and the Monroe County Historical Society has kept it standing and cared-for. Come with a camera. It sits in a cluster of Monroe and Greenbrier bridges you can string into an easy afternoon loop.

Short Description: 1910 covered bridge over Laurel Creek at Lillydale, among the shortest historic spans in the state.
New Full Description: The shortest covered bridge in West Virginia, about 34 feet, tucked over Laurel Creek at Lillydale in Monroe County. Built in 1910 and restored in 2000, it's a small, red-sided span that's easy to miss and worth the stop, especially paired with the nearby Indian Creek bridge just down the road. Two of the state's covered bridges within a few miles of each other make for a natural short Monroe County ride.

Short Description: 1870 Warren-truss covered bridge over Locust Creek near Hillsboro.
New Full Description: Locust Creek is a genuine rarity: the only Warren double-intersection truss covered bridge left in West Virginia, an unusual lattice of equal triangles you won't see on any of the state's other spans. Built in 1870 by R.N. Bruce and the most remote of all West Virginia's covered bridges, it crosses Locust Creek about six miles south of Hillsboro, birthplace of author Pearl S. Buck, and it's the last covered bridge standing in Pocahontas County. A modern bridge took over the traffic in 1990; the old span was restored for foot traffic and sits far from noise and crowds. Bring your camera and your sense of direction.

Short Description: ca. 1875 Howe-truss covered bridge over the Mud River at Milton.
New Full Description: The last Howe-truss covered bridge left in West Virginia, built around 1875 over the Mud River as the town of Milton grew up around the railroad. When it finally retired from road duty, the whole bridge was moved, in 2001, to a pond at Pumpkin Park, home of the West Virginia Pumpkin Festival and the Cabell County Fair, where it's now a walk-through centerpiece. An easy stop right off US 60, and a good reason to time a visit around the fall festival.

Short Description: 1852 Long-truss bridge over the Tygart Valley River; at 286 ft the longest covered bridge in WV and a Civil War landmark.
New Full Description: The oldest and longest covered bridge in West Virginia, and the only one in the country you can still ride across on a U.S. highway, with US 250 running right through it over the Tygart Valley River. Lemuel Chenoweth built it in 1852: a 286-foot, double-barreled span framed in the Long truss style. On June 3, 1861, the Battle of Philippi, often called the first land battle of the Civil War, was fought around it, and Union troops used the bridge itself as a barracks. It nearly didn't survive the modern era; a 1989 fire took most of it, but the community rebuilt it exactly to its 1861 appearance, and crews pulled Civil War-era mine balls out of the original timbers while they worked. Ride through slow. You're crossing the same span soldiers marched over.

Short Description: 1889 Long-truss covered bridge near Sandyville in Jackson County.
New Full Description: An 1889 Long-truss span near Sandyville in Jackson County, one of the state's handful of surviving Long-truss covered bridges. A quiet rural stop in the same county as the relocated Staats Mill bridge, two Jackson County spans you can pair on one ride.

Short Description: 1881 Multiple-Kingpost covered bridge over Simpson Creek near Bridgeport.
New Full Description: A multiple-king-post span from 1881 crossing Simpson Creek near Bridgeport, one of two covered bridges surviving in Harrison County. It's close enough to the Fletcher bridge to see both in a single easy outing near Clarksburg.

Short Description: 1887 Long-truss covered bridge, relocated near Ripley at Cedar Lakes.
New Full Description: An 1887 Long-truss span built by Enoch Staats and a local crew to carry traffic over Mill Creek at Staats' water-powered mill. When a planned lake threatened to flood its original site in the 1980s, the whole bridge was carefully moved a few miles to Cedar Lakes near Ripley, in the WVU-led relocation that helped set the standard for saving the state's covered bridges. Today it crosses a quiet pond at the Cedar Lakes center, a short walk from a restored one-room schoolhouse and pioneer buildings. An easy, photogenic stop just off I-77.

Short Description: 1903 Queen-post covered bridge over the Right Fork of the West Fork River.
New Full Description: A 1903 queen-post bridge over the Right Fork of the West Fork River at Walkersville, in Lewis County. One of the younger covered bridges on the list and a peaceful central West Virginia stop on the back roads south of Weston.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Babcock State Park
Short Description: Swing framed on the Glade Creek Grist Mill, one of the most photographed spots in West Virginia; short walk from the main lot.
New Full Description: One of West Virginia's Almost Heaven swings, hand-built by Nicholas County students and placed where the state noticed people already loved the view. This one may be the most photographed of them all: it frames the Glade Creek Grist Mill, the picture-perfect water mill that stands in for West Virginia on countless calendars and postcards. A short walk from the main lot at Babcock State Park, deep in New River Gorge country.

The park runs seasonally, roughly May through October, so plan around the boat schedule. Note: the map pin is the mainland ferry landing; the swing itself is on the island.

New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing with an expansive view over Bluestone Lake at Bluestone State Park. Pull off Route 20 near Lilly's Bridge and follow the short walk to the overlook.

Short Description: Cacapon Mountain Overlook with endless mountain views; swing closed seasonally Nov 1-Mar 31.

Time it right: the swing is closed for the season each year from November 1 to March 31. It's the closest swing to the DC and Baltimore areas, and a natural anchor for an Eastern Panhandle ride.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Chief Logan State Park
Short Description: Mountain views beside the Chief Logan Lodge; short walk from the parking area.
Address: 376 Little Buffalo Creek Rd, Logan, WV 25601
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing with mountain views beside the lodge at Chief Logan State Park near Logan, a short walk from the parking area. A convenient stop in the heart of Hatfield-McCoy country.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Droop Mountain Battlefield State Park
Short Description: Set in a Civil War battlefield park near the lookout tower; the site of WV's largest Civil War battle.
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing set within Droop Mountain Battlefield State Park, near the lookout tower and the site of the largest Civil War battle fought in West Virginia. Ridge-and-valley views in every direction, with a layer of history most swings don't have.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Lost River State Park

New Full Description: This Almost Heaven swing sits at the Cranny Crow Overlook in Lost River State Park, reached by the White Oak Trail, roughly a 4-mile out-and-back to panoramic Hardy County views. The most earned view in the set: you hike for this one, and it pays off. The map pin marks the park; the overlook is up the trail.

New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing in the 'Jug Handle' area off Main Park Road at North Bend State Park, also reachable via the Southern Railroad and Castle Rock trails. Rail-trail country in the Mid-Ohio Valley, and an easy stop off the North Bend Rail Trail.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Pipestem Resort State Park

New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing with a vista of rolling hills near the main parking area at Pipestem Resort State Park, one of the state's flagship resort parks, with an aerial tram and deep gorge views close by.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Stonewall Resort State Park
Short Description: Tranquil Stonewall Jackson Lake views behind the main lodge via the Bright Star Park Trail.
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing with tranquil views over Stonewall Jackson Lake, tucked behind the main lodge at Stonewall Resort State Park via the Bright Star Park Trail. A short, pretty walk in the Mountain Lakes region near Weston.

New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing overlooking Summersville Lake, the clear, cliff-lined water nicknamed the 'Little Bahamas of the East,' at West Virginia's newest state park. A short uphill walk from the lot delivers one of the best lake views in the state.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Tu-Endie-Wei State Park

New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing at the confluence of the Kanawha and Ohio rivers in Tu-Endie-Wei State Park at Point Pleasant, with the Silver Memorial Bridge as the backdrop. One of the smallest and most historic parks in the state, right at the water's edge.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Tygart Lake State Park
Short Description: At the Tygart Dam Overlook with a view down the 10-mile lake; parking right at the overlook.
Address: 1240 Paul E Malone Rd, Grafton, WV 26354
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing at the Tygart Dam Overlook, with a view down the 10-mile lake at Tygart Lake State Park near Grafton. Parking is right at the overlook, so the view comes easy.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Tomlinson Run State Park
Short Description: At the end of the ADA-accessible Jody Hulka Trail in WV's northernmost park.
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing at the end of the ADA-accessible Jody Hulka Trail in Tomlinson Run State Park, West Virginia's northernmost park, up at the tip of the Northern Panhandle. An accessible walk to a quiet overlook.

Business Name: Almost Heaven Swing - Valley Falls State Park
Short Description: Overlooks the cascades of Valley Falls, a stop on the WV Waterfall Trail; cross the bridge and follow the paved path.
New Full Description: An Almost Heaven swing overlooking the cascades of Valley Falls, a stop on the West Virginia Waterfall Trail, at Valley Falls State Park near Fairmont. Cross the bridge and follow the paved path to reach it.

Short Description: Roadside overlook above Summersville Lake — West Virginia's largest lake, known for some of the clearest, deepest-blue water in the eastern United States.
Meta Description: Overlook above Summersville Lake, West Virginia's largest lake, in Nicholas County.
New Full Description: An overlook at the Summersville Dam with a wide view across Summersville Lake, the largest lake in West Virginia (about 2,700 acres, 60 miles of shoreline) and a favorite of boaters and divers for its exceptionally clear water and sandstone cliffs. An easy roadside stop with parking.

Short Description: State park in Ansted with a canyon-rim overlook high above the New River Gorge.
Meta Description: Hawks Nest State Park in Ansted, WV: canyon-rim overlook, tramway, and lodge above the New River Gorge.
New Full Description: Hawks Nest State Park sits on the rim of the New River Gorge near Ansted, with an overlook offering long views down the gorge. The park includes an aerial tramway down to the river, a lodge, and hiking trails.

Short Description: A wide, roadside waterfall on the Kanawha River at Glen Ferris — no hiking required.
Meta Description: Kanawha Falls: a wide roadside waterfall on the Kanawha River near Glen Ferris, WV.
New Full Description: Kanawha Falls is a broad, low waterfall on the Kanawha River just below where the New and Gauley rivers meet, viewable from a pull-off near Glen Ferris with no trail or hike required.

Business Name: Fayette Station Road & Tunney Hunsaker Bridge
Short Description: A steep, switchbacked road descending into the New River Gorge to a river-level bridge beneath the New River Gorge Bridge.
Meta Description: Fayette Station Road: switchbacks into the New River Gorge to a river-level bridge below the arch, WV.
New Full Description: Fayette Station Road is the historic route into the New River Gorge, descending a series of tight switchbacks to the Tunney Hunsaker Bridge at river level — directly beneath the New River Gorge Bridge arch high overhead. Narrow and winding; a slow, scenic drive.

Short Description: A National Scenic Byway through the historic coal-mining communities of southern West Virginia.
Meta Description: Coal Heritage Trail: National Scenic Byway through southern West Virginia's historic coalfields.
New Full Description: The Coal Heritage Trail is a National Scenic Byway winding through the coalfields of southern West Virginia, passing coal-era towns and company-store landmarks that tell the story of the region that powered a country.

Short Description: State park home to the Glade Creek Grist Mill, purported to be the most photographed spot in West Virginia.
Meta Description: Babcock State Park, WV: home of the Glade Creek Grist Mill, trails, and forested ridges.
New Full Description: Babcock State Park near Clifftop features the Glade Creek Grist Mill — a working gristmill built in 1976 from parts of three historic West Virginia mills, and widely called the state's most photographed landmark — along with streams, forested ridges, and hiking trails.

Short Description: The Mid-Ohio Valley's authorized Harley-Davidson dealer in Williamstown — service, parts, and gear right off I-77 at the Ohio line.
New Full Description: Mothman Harley-Davidson is the Mid-Ohio Valley's authorized Harley-Davidson dealership, with factory-trained techs and full diagnostic equipment to keep your bike running right, plus a deep selection of motorcycles, parts, accessories, and apparel. An easy service stop or gear run near the Ohio River in Williamstown, just off I-77 at the state line.

Short Description: Full Harley-Davidson dealer in Morgantown, right off I-79 Exit 155 - bikes, parts, service, and gear.
New Full Description: Triple S Harley-Davidson is a 40,000-square-foot dealership in Morgantown, just off I-79 at Exit 155, with a big inventory of new and used Harleys plus MotorClothes, parts, and accessories. Known for bike nights and events, and a handy full-service stop in Mountaineer Country - it sits on the only Willie G Avenue in the world.

Short Description: Family-run Harley-Davidson dealer near Bridgeport - sales, service, parts, and gear, in business since 1977.
New Full Description: RG's Almost Heaven Harley-Davidson is a long-running, family-owned dealership on Murphys Run Road near Bridgeport, handling Harley sales, service, parts, accessories, and apparel. Riders single out the sales crew for treating you like a person, not a transaction - an easy service or gear stop in Mountaineer Country off I-79.

Short Description: Lakefront motel in Ghent with an on-site pub and grill, a mile from Winterplace - an affordable base in the New River area.
New Full Description: Skyline Lodge is a lakefront motel just off I-77 in Ghent, with rustic rooms, an on-site pub and grill, and a private lake, set in the heart of southern WV's adventure country - within about half an hour of whitewater, ATV trails, and Winterplace. An easy, affordable overnight for New River Gorge and coalfields riding.

Short Description: Historic 1857 inn on Kingwood's Main Street, with its own restaurant and bar - a characterful Preston County overnight.
New Full Description: The Preston County Inn is a Civil War-era brick house on Main Street in Kingwood, with a handful of guest rooms upstairs and a full restaurant - three dining rooms and a bistro lounge - below. Free breakfast, pet-friendly, and a genuine sense of place. A good base for Coopers Rock and Cheat Lake country in Mountaineer Country.

Short Description: Family-owned Harley-Davidson dealer in downtown Bluefield - the southern-WV service and gear stop.
New Full Description: Cole Harley-Davidson is a family-owned dealership on Bland Street in Bluefield, serving southern West Virginia with new and used Harleys, a full service department, parts, and MotorClothes. Smaller and personal by design - a friendly stop near the Virginia line and the Bluefield end of the coalfields riding.

Short Description: Home of the world's largest steerable radio telescope, deep in the National Radio Quiet Zone - tours, a science center, and no cell signal.
New Full Description: Green Bank Observatory in Pocahontas County is home to the Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope, the world's largest fully steerable radio telescope. Take a guided bus tour of the dishes, explore the hands-on science center, and grab a bite at the Starlight Cafe. Heads up for riders: you're in the heart of the National Radio Quiet Zone, so there's no cell service - download your maps before you get here.

Short Description: Harley-Davidson dealer at the Highlands near Wheeling - bikes, service, parts, and gear in the Northern Panhandle.
New Full Description: Valley Harley-Davidson sits at the Highlands in Triadelphia, just outside Wheeling, with new and used Harleys, MotorClothes, parts, and factory-trained service. A convenient Northern Panhandle stop close to I-70 and the Ohio and Pennsylvania lines.

Short Description: Creekside BBQ joint on Rt 33 east of Elkins - smoked meats, full bar, craft beer, and live music on the deck.
New Full Description: Smoke on the Water is a BBQ restaurant on Route 33 east of Elkins, with a deck overlooking Isner Creek, a full bar with local craft beer, and live music most weekends. Ribs, brisket, and pulled pork are the draw, with seafood, burgers, and pizza rounding out the menu - a relaxed refuel in the Potomac Highlands. Open Wednesday through Sunday.

Short Description: Cabins, RV, and tent sites a mile from the New River Gorge Bridge - Amish-built cabins and a general store with hand-dipped ice cream.
New Full Description: Bear Mountain Cabins & Campground sits on Laurel Creek Road off Rt 19 in Fayetteville, a mile from the New River Gorge Bridge, with Amish-built cabins, a rustic log home, and RV and tent sites among shaded woods. There's a small general store with hand-dipped ice cream, and downtown Fayetteville - one of 'America's coolest small towns' - is minutes away. A relaxed base for New River Gorge riding.

Short Description: Award-winning Harley-Davidson dealer in downtown Huntington - and yes, there's an in-store diner.
New Full Description: Black Sheep Harley-Davidson takes up about half a city block in downtown Huntington, with a big showroom of new and used Harleys, a two-floor MotorClothes department, a full service shop with a performance dyno, and its own in-store diner. A genuine destination stop in the Metro Valley near the Ohio and Kentucky lines.

Short Description: Quiet family campground two miles from the New River Gorge Bridge, off Rt 19 - RV, tent, and rustic cabin sites.
New Full Description: Rifrafters is a quiet, shady family-owned campground on Laurel Creek Road off Rt 19, two miles south of the New River Gorge Bridge, with RV sites (big-rig friendly), tent sites, and seven rustic cabins. Central to the New River Gorge's rafting and climbing scene, with a clean bathhouse and laundry - an easy overnight base for gorge-country riding.

Short Description: Rider-favorite motor inn on Rt 219 near Marlinton, 25 miles south of Snowshoe - pool, lounge, and mountain views.
New Full Description: The Marlinton Motor Inn sits on Route 219 (Seneca Trail) just outside Marlinton, about 25 miles south of Snowshoe, with a big block of rooms, a seasonal outdoor pool, and a lounge. A longtime favorite of touring riders working the scenic Pocahontas County roads - reviewers mention the staff even keep rags on hand for wiping down bikes.

Short Description: Ride a historic Shay steam locomotive up to Bald Knob through a preserved logging-town state park near Snowshoe.
New Full Description: Cass Scenic Railroad State Park preserves an original early-1900s logging town and its steep-grade Shay steam locomotives, which now haul visitors up the mountain to Bald Knob for big highland views. The restored company houses rent as lodging, there's a museum, a restaurant (the Last Run), and bike rentals - a full-day destination in the Potomac Highlands near Snowshoe. Train season runs roughly May through October.

Short Description: Famously wacky hot dog joint on the Ohio River in Lesage - school-bus dining rooms, junkyard decor, and the giant 'Homewrecker' dog.
New Full Description: Hillbilly Hotdogs is a beloved roadside oddity on Ohio River Road in Lesage, packed with junkyard-chic decor and old school buses turned into dining rooms. It's built its reputation on over-the-top hot dogs - the 15-inch 'Homewrecker' is the challenge - and earned a national following after appearing on Food Network. A genuine only-in-WV stop near Huntington, and the batch's most-mentioned pick.

Short Description: Coffee, breakfast, and lunch inside a converted 120-year-old church in downtown Fayetteville - a New River Gorge staple.
New Full Description: The Cathedral Cafe fills a former downtown Fayetteville church with stained glass, book-lined shelves, and an all-day breakfast and lunch menu. It's an easy, popular stop right in the heart of New River Gorge riding - coffee and a bagel before a gorge run, or a loaded sandwich after. Fresh, homemade, and unmistakably local; expect a line on weekends.

Short Description: Hot dogs, burgers, and blended ice-cream 'storms' a half-mile from Summersville Lake and the Gauley - a warm-weather rider refuel.
Address: 2243 Summersville Lake Rd, Mount Nebo, WV 26679
New Full Description: Fat Eddie's is a cheerful walk-up spot just off the Summersville Lake dam, known for hot dogs, burgers, and its blended ice-cream 'storms.' Half a mile from the lake and close to the Gauley, it's an easy warm-weather refuel on a Nicholas County ride. Note it's seasonal - open roughly March through October.

Short Description: Third-generation Swiss-American restaurant in the tiny mountain village of Helvetia - worth the twisty ride in.
New Full Description: The Hutte has served Swiss-American food from the Swiss-settled village of Helvetia since 1968, in an antique-filled century-old farmhouse. Roesti, sauerbraten, homemade bread, and a locally-famous peach cobbler are the draw - and the curvy Randolph County roads in are half the reason to go. Hours are limited (generally Thursday through Sunday); reservations are wise for groups.

Short Description: Live-music venue, bar, and deli-cafe in the old DePollo store in historic Thomas - Canaan country's social hub.
New Full Description: The Purple Fiddle packs the old DePollo General Store in Thomas with touring bands most weekends, plus a deli menu of sandwiches, wraps, soups, local ice cream, and the area's best beer list. It's the social anchor of the Thomas and Canaan arts scene and an easy detour off the Rt 32/48 highlands routes. Family-friendly, all ages, open Wednesday through Sunday.

Short Description: Family-owned authentic Mexican in Kingwood with Cheat River and golf-course views - right by the Preston County Inn.
New Full Description: Rosemary's Thyme has served made-from-scratch Mexican food in Kingwood since 2015 - fajitas, tacos, and margaritas with a view over the Cheat River and golf course. It sits in the same Preston County town as the Preston County Inn, making the two an easy overnight-and-dinner pairing for Coopers Rock and Cheat Lake riding.

Short Description: Homecooked diner and famous pie at the foot of Spruce Knob on US 33 - a prime Seneca Rocks corridor stop.
New Full Description: The Gateway Restaurant sits right on US 33 in Riverton, at the Brierly Gap turnoff up to Spruce Knob and minutes from Seneca Rocks. It's a plain-looking, big-hearted diner beloved for fried chicken, hearty daily specials, and homemade pies - exactly the refuel a rider wants before or after the eastern-highlands climbs. One of the best-placed food stops on the whole Seneca Rocks and Spruce Knob loop.
